healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private healthcare system. Public hospitals are free for citizens and residents. Private facilities offer faster, higher-quality care. Port of Spain General Hospital and Eric Williams Medical Sciences Complex are the main public hospitals.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is adequate in Port of Spain and San Fernando with several public and private hospitals. Private facilities offer better service and shorter wait times. Tobago has more limited options with the Scarborough General Hospital as the main facility. Specialist care is available but may have long waits in public system.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-6pm weekdays, Saturday mornings. Some pharmacies in shopping centers open later. Limited Sunday/holiday hours.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are well-stocked in urban areas. Major pharmacy chains are found in malls and commercial areas. Staff speak English. Bring prescriptions for controlled medications.
prescriptionRules: Prescription medications require a valid prescription from a licensed medical practitioner. Controlled substances are strictly regulated. Bring prescriptions from home for any medications you carry.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled narcotics (opioids)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription. Trinidad and Tobago has strict drug laws.

restrictedMeds.name: Pseudoephedrine
restrictedMeds.note: Regulated due to potential misuse. Available with pharmacist consultation.

bringDocumentation: Bring prescriptions, a doctor's letter for controlled medications, travel insurance documentation, and your health insurance card. English documentation is standard.

travelInsurance.tips: Recommended for all visitors. Private healthcare costs can add up quickly. Public hospitals may have long wait times. Ensure coverage for emergency evacuation if visiting Tobago.

recommended: Routine vaccinations (MMR, diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis, varicella, polio, flu)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers. Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Dengue and Zika are present — use insect repellent. Rainy season (June-November) increases mosquito-borne illness risk.

waterNotes: Tap water is generally safe to drink in urban areas including Port of Spain and major towns. Water quality is good and treated. Bottled water is widely available if preferred.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety is generally good at restaurants and hotels. Trinidad has a vibrant street food culture — doubles, roti, and bake & shark are popular and generally safe from established vendors. Use common sense with street food hygiene.
medicalTourismNote: Trinidad and Tobago has a small but growing medical tourism sector, particularly for dental and cosmetic procedures. Costs are lower than in North America.
sources: Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of Health
metaDescription: Trinidad and Tobago health guide: hospitals, pharmacies, vaccinations, insurance, and emergency info.

hospitals.name: Eric Williams Medical Sciences Complex (EWMSC)
hospitals.notes: Major public teaching hospital. Full emergency department. English-speaking staff. Can handle most conditions.

hospitals.name: Port of Spain General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital in the capital. Emergency services available 24/7. Can be busy with long wait times.

hospitals.name: Scarborough General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital on Tobago. Handles emergencies but complex cases may be transferred to Trinidad.

dentalCare.availability: Good availability in Port of Spain and San Fernando with private dental clinics. Limited options on Tobago.
dentalCare.notes: Private dental care is of good quality and affordable compared to North America. Public dental clinics have long wait times.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, visit a private dental clinic in Port of Spain or the emergency department of a major hospital.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: Contact the Lifeline crisis center at +1-868-645-2800
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available. English is the primary language. Several private psychologists and psychiatrists practice in Port of Spain.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are available but limited compared to North America. St. Ann's Hospital in Port of Spain is the main psychiatric facility. Private therapists offer better care.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is improving but still limited in many areas. Newer buildings tend to have better access.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals have basic wheelchair access. Older facilities may have limitations.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public transport (maxi-taxis) is not wheelchair accessible. Private taxis are the best option.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact hotels in advance about accessibility. Beach areas vary in accessibility. The main tourist areas in Tobago have limited wheelchair access.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mandatory mask requirements. May be requested in healthcare facilities.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at public hospitals and private labs throughout Trinidad.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare system has returned to normal operations. Standard hygiene precautions recommended.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private facilities typically require upfront payment by credit card or cash. Obtain itemized receipts and a medical report. Public hospitals may be free or low-cost. Submit claims to your travel insurer with all documentation upon return.

commonCosts.currency: TTD (Trinidad and Tobago Dollar), prices shown in USD equivalent
commonCosts.note: Public hospitals are free or very low-cost for emergency care. Private facilities are more expensive but still affordable by North American standards.

medicalEvacuation.note: Evacuation to Miami is the standard route for conditions requiring advanced care. Trinidad has adequate facilities for most emergencies but limited specialist capabilities.

pharmacyChains.name: SuperPharm
pharmacyChains.where: Multiple locations across Trinidad; found in major malls and commercial areas

drugNameMap.note: Widely available OTC at all pharmacies. Panadol is a popular brand.
Available OTC at pharmacies throughout the country.
